Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service San Diego CA
805 AM PST Mon Nov 23 2026

.SYNOPSIS...
Widespread coastal flooding is expected this week due to King 
Tides and increased surf. Showers may continue past sunrise this 
morning, mainly for coastal areas of San Diego County and southern
portions of San Diego County from the coast to the mountains. 
Tuesday will be warmer with weak offshore flow. Winds will weaken 
on Wednesday. Thanksgiving and Friday will be dry and warmer with 
northeast winds gusting to 35 mph along and below the coastal 
slopes of the mountains. There will be a cooling trend for next 
weekend with the next chance for precipitation for late Sunday 
into Monday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO
COUNTIES...

...UPDATED AVIATION DISCUSSION...

.SHORT TERM (Today through Wednesday)...
Showers may continue past sunrise this morning, mainly for the
coastal waters into coastal areas of San Diego County and across 
southern portions of San Diego County from the coast to the 
mountains. Rainfall will be mostly less than 0.10 inch with 
isolated rainfall to around 0.25 inch.

High temperatures on Tuesday will be a few degrees warmer, around
5 to locally 10 degrees warmer from the coast to the coastal
slopes of the mountains, around 5 degrees above average near the
coast. High temperatures on Tuesday will be mostly in the lower 
to mid 70s for the coast and valleys. There will be weak offshore 
flow on Tuesday with northeast winds along and below the coastal 
slopes of the mountains mostly 25 mph or less.

A weakening low pressure system moving inland across California on
Wednesday may cool the coast and valleys slightly with the 
deserts onto the desert slopes of the mountains a few to around 5 
degrees warmer.

&&

.LONG TERM (Thanksgiving through Sunday)...

Thanksgiving and Friday will be dry and warmer with northeast 
winds gusting to 35 mph along and below the coastal slopes of the 
mountains. High temperatures on Thanksgiving will warm around 5
degrees for the deserts onto the desert slopes of the mountains
and 5 to 10 degrees from the coastal slopes of the mountains to
the coast with warmest high temperatures in the lower 80s for the
lower deserts and for inland coastal areas into the western
valleys.

There will be additional warming on Friday of a few to around 5
degrees with warmest high temperatures on Friday in the lower to
mid 80s for the lower deserts and for inland coastal areas into
the western valleys.

Onshore flow will return for Saturday into next week. High
temperatures for the coast and valleys will cool around 5 degrees
on Saturday from the coast to the mountains. There will be
additional cooling of high temperatures on Sunday of around 5
degrees near the coast to 5 to 10 degrees for the mountains. 
High temperatures on Sunday will range from the mid to upper 60s
for the far inland valleys to the lower 70s for the coast into the
western valleys.

The next chance for precipitation will be for late Sunday into
Monday with the chance for measurable precipitation from the coast
to the mountains around 50 percent and the chance for 0.5 inch or
more of rainfall ranging from 10 to 15 percent near the coast to
around 25 percent for the mountains

&&

.AVIATION... 
231605Z...FEW-SCT050-070 through 21Z...with FEW-SCT250 expected
after 21Z. No significant wind issues. 

&&

.MARINE...
No marine hazards are expected through Tuesday.

A large, long period west swell will arrive Wednesday afternoon 
and build into Thursday, bringing combined seas of 8-12 feet. 
Northwest winds briefly reach 20-25 kt in the outer coastal waters
near San Clemente Island Wednesday afternoon and evening. The 
combination of large seas and breezy winds will create conditions 
hazardous to small craft. Seas begin to Thursday afternoon, falling 
below 10 ft by Thursday evening.

&&

.BEACHES...
Morning high tides will increase this week, and have already reached 
7.35 feet (MLLW) on Sunday at La Jolla. Highest tides will occur 
Tuesday through Thursday at 7.9-8.3 feet, peaking on Wednesday. 
These forecast tides have been adjusted 1.1-1.2 feet above 
baseline astronomical predictions based on trends in recent 
observations, and will likely break the all time tidal records 
recently set in late October. 

Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet 
through Wednesday morning, but an incoming west swell of 8-9 ft at 
18-19 seconds arrives late Wednesday into Thursday. This 
will generate large breaking waves of 6-8 feet on Thursday, with 
sets of 10-12 feet on exposed west-facing beaches. Surf lowers to 3-
6 feet on Friday.

The combination of forecast record high tides and elevated surf 
will likely lead to moderate to locally major coastal flooding 
through Tuesday. A Coastal Flood Advisory remains in effect through 
early Tuesday morning. King Tides Tue-Thu combined with elevated to 
high surf will likely result in major coastal flooding, with locally 
extreme flooding expected on Thursday. A Coastal Flood Warning 
remains in effect from Tuesday morning through early Friday 
afternoon.

&&

.SKYWARN... 
Skywarn activation is not requested. However weather spotters are
encouraged to report significant weather conditions.
